ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that $\triangle ABC$ is an equilateral triangle with a side length of 10. $D$ is the midpoint of $AC$, $\angle EDF=120^\circ$, $DE$ intersects line segment $AB$ at $E$, and $DF$ intersects the extension of $BC$ at $F$. If $AE=4BE$, then what is the length of $CF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, construct $DM\parallel BC$ intersecting $AB$ at $M$, \\
$\because$ $AE=4BE$, \\
$\therefore$ $BE=\frac{1}{5}AB=2$, \\
$\because$ $D$ is the midpoint of $AC$, and $\triangle ABC$ is an equilateral triangle, \\
$\therefore$ $MD$ is the median of $\triangle ABC$, \\
$\therefore$ $MD=DC=BM=\frac{1}{2}BC=5$, $\angle DME=120^\circ=\angle DCF$, $\angle ADM=60^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $ME=BM-BE=3$, $\angle MDC=120^\circ$, \\
$\because$ $\angle EDF=120^\circ$, $\angle MDC-\angle EDC=\angle EDF-\angle EDC$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle MDE=\angle CDF$, \\
In $\triangle DEM$ and $\triangle DFC$, \\
$\because$ $\left\{\begin{array}{l}\angle MDE=\angle CDF \\ \angle DME=\angle DCF \\ DM=DC \end{array}\right.$, \\
$\therefore$ $\triangle DEM\cong \triangle DFC\left(AAS\right)$, \\
$\therefore$ $CF=ME=\boxed{3}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a triangle ABC, with A above, B at the lower left, and C at the lower right; D is located on side AC, and E is located on side AB; a line segment DE is drawn from E to D, and a line is drawn from D toward the lower right to intersect the extension line of BC at F, with F on the right side of C, conforming to the structure in the problem statement that DE intersects AB at E and DF intersects the extension line of BC at F. Reasoning: According to the specified method, through D draw DM∥BC, intersecting AB at M. From AE=4BE and AB=10, we get AE+BE=10, so 5BE=10, BE=2. Because D is the midpoint of AC, and DM∥BC, by the property of the midline of a triangle, M is the midpoint of AB, BM=5, and DM=BC/2=5; at the same time DC=AC/2=5. Thus ME=BM−BE=5−2=3. Since ABC is an equilateral triangle and DM∥BC, we can get ∠DME=120°, and also because CF is on the extension line of BC, ∠DCF=120°; and ∠MDC=120°. Given ∠EDF=120°, subtracting the common angle ∠EDC from ∠MDC and ∠EDF at the same time, we obtain ∠MDE=∠CDF. Thus in △DEM and △DFC, ∠MDE=∠CDF, ∠DME=∠DCF, DM=DC, so the two triangles are congruent. Corresponding side CF=ME=3.
